title: Meridian Workstation Intrusion
description: Investigate a fake remote-support incident from initial access through persistence and lateral movement.
safety: The attacker domains and public IPs in this question set are fictional or documentation-range indicators. Do not resolve, browse to, or contact them.

questions.title: Patient zero
questions.prompt: Which workstation was compromised first?
questions.hint: Establish the earliest abnormal activity before following later spread.

questions.title: First affected identity
questions.prompt: Which domain user owned the first suspicious process tree?
questions.hint: Attribute the earliest suspicious process tree, not the later remote logons.

questions.title: Copied trouble
questions.prompt: What social-engineering technique caused the victim to paste and execute the initial command?
questions.hint: The initial execution leaves evidence in more than one telemetry source.

questions.title: The download interpreter
questions.prompt: Which command interpreter did Explorer launch to retrieve and unpack the initial bundle?
questions.hint: Correlate the user's execution history with the earliest suspicious process tree.

questions.title: Loader on disk
questions.prompt: What exact filename did the signed portable interpreter use on disk?
questions.hint: Follow the extraction and execution lineage carefully.

questions.title: Loader identity
questions.prompt: What original filename was embedded in that signed executable?
questions.hint: The displayed filename is not the binary's original identity.

questions.title: Path configuration pivot
questions.prompt: What exact Python path-configuration filename was placed beside the portable interpreter?
questions.hint: Review all files created in the runtime directory immediately before execution.

questions.title: Sidecar import
questions.prompt: What exact sidecar archive filename supplied the loader's startup code?
questions.hint: Not every archive advertises its format through its extension.

questions.title: First payload
questions.prompt: What exact executable did the signed loader start to establish the first foothold?
questions.hint: Follow the disguised interpreter's direct child.

questions.title: Direct discovery
questions.prompt: Which two native executables were repeatedly launched directly to collect identity and network configuration?
questions.hint: Compare recurring child-process patterns across the affected hosts.

questions.title: System inventory chain
questions.prompt: Which parent-child executable pair was used to collect operating-system inventory? Submit the pair in execution order.
questions.hint: One member of the pair is only a wrapper for the other.

questions.title: Support tool unmasked
questions.prompt: What remote-support product was deployed under the same support-themed executable name?
questions.hint: A reused display name hides two different binary identities.

questions.title: Hands on keyboard
questions.prompt: What exact command line was entered through the visible remote-support session to open the diagnostic shell?
questions.hint: Separate interactive operator activity from automated discovery.

questions.title: A trusted process turns
questions.prompt: Which legitimate executable loaded user-profile DLLs, spawned discovery processes, and made an unusual outbound connection?
questions.hint: Correlate module loads, child processes, and network behavior.

questions.title: Logon foothold
questions.prompt: What user-level registry value was created for persistence? Submit the key path including its value name.
questions.hint: Endpoint registry telemetry names user hives by SID rather than HKCU.

questions.title: User-profile plugins
questions.prompt: Which two exact DLL filenames were staged in the user-writable plugin directory?
questions.hint: Focus on new user-profile modules associated with the persistent process.

questions.title: The sprayed secret
questions.prompt: What organization-themed password was tested against several domain identities?
questions.hint: Inspect the credential-use activity that precedes lateral access.

questions.title: Rejected user accounts
questions.prompt: Which two ordinary user accounts rejected the sprayed password?
questions.hint: Separate ordinary-user failures from the other authentication attempts.

questions.title: Rejected privileged account
questions.prompt: Which administrator-named account also rejected the sprayed password?
questions.hint: One failed identity is named for a privileged role.

questions.title: The credential that worked
questions.prompt: Which account accepted the password and enabled lateral movement?
questions.hint: Look for the successful authentication that follows the failures.

questions.title: The second foothold
questions.prompt: Which workstation was compromised through lateral movement?
questions.hint: Trace the successful credential use to its resulting foothold.

questions.title: Movement utility
questions.prompt: Which remote service-execution utility performed the lateral movement?
questions.hint: Correlate execution on the source with service activity on the target.

questions.title: Remote share trail
questions.prompt: Which two administrative SMB shares show credential testing and remote payload staging?
questions.hint: Different stages of the movement use different remote shares.

questions.title: Service residue
questions.prompt: What exact service name was installed on the lateral-movement target?
questions.hint: Distinguish the installed service name from its binary path.

questions.title: Privilege on arrival
questions.prompt: Under which security principal did the payload run on the second workstation?
questions.hint: Use the effective identity on the target, not the credential used in transit.

questions.title: Attacker domains
questions.prompt: Which two attacker-controlled domains appear in the intrusion?
questions.hint: Separate rare intrusion-related destinations from routine services.

questions.title: Infrastructure mapping
questions.prompt: Map each attacker domain to its resolved public IP address.
questions.hint: Pair name resolution with the connections that follow it.

questions.title: Implant channel
questions.prompt: Which destination port was used for the implant command-and-control channel?
questions.hint: Separate payload traffic from the remote-support traffic.

questions.title: Remote-support signaling and relay
questions.prompt: Which two destination ports carried remote-support signaling and relay traffic?
questions.hint: Count only completed connections from the client process; ignore attempts that were never answered.

questions.title: Additional remote-support connection
questions.prompt: Which additional destination port did the remote-support client successfully connect to?
questions.hint: Review the complete connection set rather than only the long-lived channels.

questions.title: Footholds calling home
questions.prompt: Which two workstations generated implant callbacks to the attacker infrastructure?
questions.hint: Confirm the originating endpoints rather than relying on intermediary network traffic.
